record.title: Qingdao Port report describes AI berth scheduling in routine use with reported planning time falling to minutes
record.summary: A Chinese-language report published on 10 October quotes a Qingdao Port automation-control center director describing a berth-planning agent built around 132 operational factors. The report says plan preparation moved from hours to minutes and that the berth agent was in routine operation with recommendation adoption above 90%. This is a second-hand media account hosted by Shandong’s propaganda department, not a port-owned technical record. The adoption figure is not plan accuracy or an independently measured productivity gain.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: A 10 October Chinese-language report credited to Dazhong News and hosted by Shandong Propaganda Department quotes a Qingdao Port automation-control center director describing a berth-planning agent that includes 132 factors and is in routine operation.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The quoted director says plan preparation changed from hour-scale to minute-scale and reported recommendation adoption is above 90%; the report does not give a denominator or observation window.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The source does not establish plan accuracy, improved throughput, lower cost, causal effect, independent measurement or generalization to other ports.

evidence_gaps.description: No port-owned technical or operations record with a reproducible system description and metric definitions was recovered.
The report supplies no matched baseline, plan accuracy, throughput, cost or safety outcomes; adoption alone does not establish productivity or causal impact.

brief.importance_rationale: If accurate, a domain-model-plus-agent scheduling system in port operations could change dispatch workflow and labor/throughput decisions at a major logistics node. This is a meaningful deployment signal, but it rests on second-hand reporting and has no auditable performance or economic measurement.
limitations: The page is a provincial propaganda-site republication credited to Dazhong News, not a port-owned technical report; its staff quotation remains a reported claim.
The >90% metric is recommendation adoption, not plan accuracy, and has no denominator or observation period.
The hour-to-minute statement lacks a defined baseline, task mix, sample size or comparison method.
No throughput, safety, cost, staffing, emissions or causal outcome is measured.
The Qingdao city-portal report surfaced in search was inaccessible and is not used as evidence.
brief.summary: A Chinese-language report published on 10 October quotes a Qingdao Port automation-control center director describing a berth-planning agent built around 132 operational factors. The report says plan preparation moved from hours to minutes and that the berth agent was in routine operation with recommendation adoption above 90%. This is a second-hand media account hosted by Shandong’s propaganda department, not a port-owned technical record. The adoption figure is not plan accuracy or an independently measured productivity gain.

technical.claimed_result: The quoted director says berth-plan preparation moved from hour-scale to minute-scale and the berth agent is in routine operation with recommendation adoption above 90%. These are reported claims with no denominator, measurement window, matched baseline or independent audit.
technical.compute_or_cost: No model-serving, integration, staffing, infrastructure or lifecycle cost data are reported.
technical.demonstrated_result: The accessible Chinese-language report, hosted by Shandong Propaganda Department and credited to Dazhong News, quotes a Qingdao Port automation-control center director about the system and reported routine operation. This demonstrates the content and attribution of the report, not the underlying system performance.
technical.implementation_status: Reported by the source as in routine operation; no port-owned technical documentation, logs or independent site verification were inspected.
technical.mechanism: The report describes a Star Harbor port-domain model connected to berth, equipment and yard agents and a knowledge base. It says a berth-planning agent incorporates 132 operational factors; the detailed underlying model, data, integrations and safety controls are not published in the inspected source.
technical.novelty: A report of a port-domain model connected to task-specific berth, equipment and yard agents, with claimed operational use for berth planning.
technical.regime: Qingdao Port dry-bulk berth planning, as described by a 10 October 2026 Dazhong News report quoting a port automation-control center director. The exact operational interval, number/type of plans and adoption denominator are not given.
technical.reproducibility: Not independently reproducible from the inspected report; no model, system description, dataset, code, plan logs or evaluation protocol is provided.
technical.strongest_baseline: The report says plan preparation previously took hours; it does not describe the prior workflow quantitatively or provide a matched comparison.

brief.title: Qingdao Port report describes AI berth scheduling in routine use with reported planning time falling to minutes
brief.why_it_matters: If the attributed account is accurate, it is a concrete report of a domain model and task-specific agents being used in port scheduling, a high-consequence logistics setting. The bounded source establishes what the report says about operational use; it does not establish a causal productivity gain, accuracy improvement, cost reduction or independent validation.
